A1.justification: Both complete, readable 35-page PDFs describe the same ManyICLBench study. Main-text content and Appendices A-I can be matched reliably, including renumbered figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 12 language models, demonstration-removal and replacement experiments, and appendix error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and additionally reports the intent-classification demonstration-selection experiment in Section 7.2 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, SSL/ASL categorization, sample learning ratio, and global context index procedures remain unchanged. The added demonstration-selection conditions are analytical controls, not a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: The same datasets, task categories, languages, and benchmark subsets remain. The new analysis uses existing BANKING77 and CLINC150 tasks; its demonstration-selection variants change the experimental protocol rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4 and Figure 1 expand the preliminary comparison from ten to eleven open-weight models by including Mistral-Large-Instruct, explicitly excluded there in v2. Mistral-Large already appeared in Table 2 and Appendix H, so it is newly included in this particular comparison.

E3.justification: Section 7.2 adds a comparison of full demonstrations, removal of the closest 10%, and retention of only the closest 10% at plotted context settings from 1k to 128k. General sampling and decoding settings remain unchanged. Figure 4 labels its metric accuracy, without reconciling this with Section 3.1's macro-F1 specification for classification.

E4.justification: The new intent-classification ablation tests whether a small relevant subset is sufficient, extending v2's removal and replacement tests of retrieval dependence. Existing quantization, duplicate-versus-unique demonstration, and ASL error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds. Existing error-bar displays remain unchanged, and v3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test.

E6.justification: Figure 1 substantially revises retained-model scores and correlations, changing some long-context trends: Jamba-1.5-Mini's plotted science score at 128k changes from about 37 to 56, removing the earlier collapse. Mistral-Large aggregates are added, and Figure 4 newly reports that the closest 10% approaches full-demonstration performance around 64k. Tables 2-3 and appendix results remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the Figure 1 revisions as reruns or setting changes.

T1.justification: The SLR definition in Equation 1, replacement-based ratio in Appendix F, and global context index in Appendix G are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about task-dependent many-shot benefits, SSL versus ASL, and long-context performance degradation remain. v3 explicitly describes the benchmark as built from existing tasks, which v2 already established through its task-selection discussion.

C2.justification: Section 7.2 adds an interpretation of retrieval sufficiency. The limitations discussion newly acknowledges untested data contamination but argues that conclusions remain valid regardless of prior data exposure, attributing degradation to long-context handling. This adds a substantive, experimentally unverified qualification and causal argument.

D1.justification: Section 3 explicitly limits the above-50B quantization statement to open-weight models, and Section 5 explains that resource constraints motivated the SLR model subset. These are limited documentation clarifications; appendix implementation information, prompt examples, and code/data access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. Section 3.1 adds explicit attribution for task selection, while Section 7.2 connects its new findings to the 5% retrieval result attributed to Bertsch et al. (2024), modestly extending the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: Several descriptive paragraphs are edited, error analysis becomes a standalone Section 7 with two subsections, acknowledgments are added, and limitations are expanded and unnumbered. Most prose and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with an additional model series and revised axes and legend, and a new two-panel Figure 4 is added. Subsequent figures are renumbered and main-text pagination shifts; existing tables and other figure contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Section 7.2 and Figure 4 strengthen retrieval-sufficiency evidence beyond v2's removal tests. However, Figure 1 changes several retained-model trends without explaining their relationship to unchanged Appendix H results, and Figure 4's accuracy label conflicts with the general macro-F1 description. The new contamination discussion also asserts validity without testing it. These benefits and unresolved reporting issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
